status.en: 149 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 27% fewer than the week before, most of them in Abuja, Lagos and Kaduna.
status.nb: 149 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 27 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Abuja, Lagos og Kaduna.

summary.en: Bandits in Zamfara have burned families alive and abducted residents, while gunmen killed a security volunteer and 11 of his relatives and seized 13 people in the same state. In Plateau, terrorists attacked two communities, killing five and injuring two, and later a fresh assault killed a soldier and three locals. In Delta, motorcyclists demanded justice after a colleague was killed at a rally, and in Ogun police rescued ten abducted passengers and killed a suspected kidnapper in a gun battle. The conflict recorded 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Banditter i Zamfara har brent familier levende og bortført innbyggere, mens væpnede menn drepte en sikkerhetsfrivillig og 11 av hans slektninger og tok 13 personer som gisler i samme delstat. I Plateau angrep terrorister to lokalsamfunn, drepte fem og såret to, og senere drepte et nytt angrep en soldat og tre lokale. I Delta krevde motorsyklister rettferdighet etter at en kollega ble drept på en samling, og i Ogun reddet politiet ti bortførte passasjerer og drepte en mistenkt kidnapper i en skuddveksling. Konflikten registrerte 1 486 dødsfall i kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
